Latin word

plērumque

adverb

generally, as a rule, mostly; mostly, for the most part, usually; usually, as a rule, for the most part

In this lexicon

  • in general

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.118: plērumque autem parentium praeceptīs imbūtī; Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: plērumque circā hōram prīmam

  • most

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: plērumque circā hōram prīmam; Cic. Off. 1.118: plērumque autem parentium praeceptīs imbūtī

  • usually

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam; Cic. Off. 1.135: habentur autem plērumque sermōnēs aut dē domesticīs negōtiīs aut dē rē pūblicā; Traupman 401: usually, plērumque

Examples

  • ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō

    I wake when I like, generally about the first hour, often before, rarely laterPlin. Ep. 9.36.1
